input.quote: (a) Assignment. Except as stated in Sections 5.3, 7.4 and 7.6, this Agreement may not be assigned by the Depositor or the Servicer without the consent of the Owner Trustee, the Indenture Trustee, the Certificateholders and the Noteholders of at least 66-2/3% of the Note Balance of the Controlling Class.
input.rationale: Section 10.2(a) imposes a symmetrical assignment restriction on the Depositor (our party) and the Servicer (Cellco), and expressly carves out Sections 5.3, 7.4 and 7.6. Section 5.3 gives us the full preferred carve-out: any Person into which the Depositor is merged or consolidated, resulting from such a merger, succeeding to the Depositor's business, or that is an Affiliate to whom the Depositor has assigned the Agreement automatically becomes the successor Depositor, with no counterparty consent required — only post-closing assumption/opinion/notice mechanics within fifteen Business Days. Section 7.6 mirrors this for the Servicer, so the arrangement is mutual. Cellco cannot exit: Section 7.1 (No Resignation) bars the Servicer from resigning unless it is legally unable to perform, and there is no change-of-control (or "deemed assignment") trigger anywhere in the document giving the Servicer a termination, re-pricing or fee-reset right on our change of control — searches for "change of control" and "may not assign" return no such provision. Two minor sub-elements fall short of the ideal preferred wording and are noted rather than flagged: the residual consent standard for non-carve-out assignments is absolute rather than "not to be unreasonably withheld," and there is no express bar on assignment to a competitor. Neither is material here — the residual consent runs to the Owner Trustee, Indenture Trustee, Certificateholders and 66-2/3% of the Controlling Class (structural noteholder protection benefiting the Issuer's capital structure, not counterparty leverage), and Section 7.4 independently controls who may succeed Cellco by requiring a $50,000,000-net-worth servicer acceptable to the Owner Trustee and Indenture Trustee. The clause therefore meets the preferred position on its material terms; no redline warranted.
